subject: Executive approval request: Pulsar-80 dedicated exception + transient burst hold (Nebula Therapeutics)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Executive approval request: Pulsar-80 dedicated exception + transient burst hold (Nebula Therapeutics)

Team,

Quick summary: Nebula Therapeutics is finalizing a 24-month Dedicated capacity contract but requires an unsupported accelerator variant (Pulsar-80) for an upcoming model tuning window. They also want a 90-day transient reservation hold (to cover a regulatory test burst) and a one-time onboarding discount that would bring effective TCV down ~25% in year one.

Why this matters: Nebula is an early strategic genomics partner — fast reference case and high likelihood of expansion into Dedicated + Private in 2029. They are requesting the Pulsar-80 because one of their training microservices depends on a vendor-supplied kernel that we haven't validated for the standard accelerator families. Our engineering team has validated functional compatibility but has requested an exception for an unlisted accelerator family due to minor kernel work that would be done post-signing.

Request (what we need from execs):
- Approval to commit a Pulsar-80 dedicated pool for 24 months (nonstandard accelerator exception)
- Approve a temporary 90-day reservation hold (no utilization penalties) beginning at contract execution
- Approve a promotional TCV discount not to exceed 25% applied to the first 12 months (finance to verify margin impact)
- Approve capped burst overage rate: $1.75/token-equivalent for the 90-day window (instead of standard $2.50)

Attachments: Nebula_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW draft), pulsar80_benchmark_results.csv (engineering checks), price_terms.xlsx (deal math)

Risks & mitigations:
- Engineering time: we've scoped a 2-week validation and a small ops playbook to limit risk.
- Preemption: we will apply soft preemption rules and a fixed burst cap to avoid noisy noisy overages.
- Contract terms: legal still needs to run a short risk addendum; procurement says they can sign within 48 hours once pricing is approved.

Ask: Can we get a one-off approval today/tomorrow? Procurement is asking for a DocuSign link by EOD Monday to hit their board window.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0136

Grace —

Thanks for the tight summary. A couple quick clarifications before I escalate to Marcus for signoff: 1) Is the 25% discount blended across token/instance charges, or is it a one-time credit? 2) Confirm the requested Pulsar-80 capacity in slot-hours (we need a numeric ask for capacity planning).

Also, please attach the benchmark notes from infra (high level) — I saw the CSV but a one-paragraph summary will help Marcus.

If you can send those in the next hour I can loop Marcus and Lauren.

—Karthik
VP, GTM Operations
[internal short sig]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Executive approval request: Pulsar-80 dedicated exception + transient burst hold (Nebula Therapeutics)

Karthik —

Answers below:
- Discount mechanics: It's a blended discount applied as a 25% reduction to committed reservation charges for the first 12-month billing period (not a one-time credit). Overages remain billable at the specified capped rate for the 90-day window.
- Capacity ask: 1200 slot-hours/month of Pulsar-80 (equivalent to a 6x small pool for our config) — ramp plan in SOW appendix A.

Bench summary (from infra): "Functional compatibility validated on internal test harness; tail latency within 12% of our nominal fleet at 2x batch sizes. We observed a single kernel fallback path that requires a micro-optimization; estimated 2 engineer-weeks to harden. Ops will treat the first 30 days as 'validation mode' with increased telemetry and an on-call runbook."

I've uploaded a single-page summary to the HubSpot deal and included the SOW/price workbook.

Grace
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@nebulatx.com>

Grace —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clarity. We are comfortable with the proposed validation cadence; our legal and procurement teams are aligned to sign once the Pulsar-80 commitment and promotional pricing are confirmed in DocuSign. The burst hold is essential for the regulatory dry-run scheduled in mid-July (we can move that to late July if you need more time).

Please mark the DocuSign envelope for me and copy procurement@nebulatx.com.

Team —

I reviewed the ask and supporting notes. I approve the following, on these conditions:

1) Approve dedicated Pulsar-80 pool for 24 months at the requested 1200 slot-hours/month.
2) Approve a promotional 25% discount applied to committed reservation charges for months 1–12, contingent on Finance signoff of margin impact (Lauren, please confirm before we send the DocuSign).
3) Approve a 90-day transient reservation hold starting at execution with a capped burst overage rate of $1.75/token-equivalent for the hold window. Any consumption beyond the documented burst cap will revert to standard overage pricing.
4) Engineering must provide a short-run runbook and a 2-week remediation plan to be attached as an addendum to the SOW. No production workload routing until remediation is complete.

Lauren: please confirm acceptance and update the DocuSign envelope with the conditional addendum. Grace: proceed to get the envelope ready and loop in Legal.

Marcus Lin
VP, Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
